subject: research/twin-recalibration
professional: a control / system-identification researcher (adaptive LQ control, experiment design) reviewing for a controls venue such as CDC or Automatica

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 10 tests OK in 4.2 s. Recomputed with a separate script (own Riccati fixed-point iteration, own finite-difference rho on the true closed-loop cost, no import of the package): k*=0.82335, J*=1.074101, rho=0.565662 (reported 0.5656), c0=4.18906, gamma=5.36316, c=9.5522 (reported 9.552); T*=40726/8774/1890/407 and N*=49.11/22.79/10.58/4.91 at qd=1e-6..1e-3 (reported 40728/8775/1890/407, 49.11/22.79/10.58/4.91; the 2-unit gap in T* is the rounding of rho in the printout); excess 0.03456/0.07444/0.16036/0.34527 (reported 0.03455/0.07444/0.16034/0.34523); equal-thirds term 0.011519/0.05346/0.11519 (reported 0.01152/0.05346/0.11517); stability cliff b_hat=0.21383 (reported 0.2138); Kalman-twin regret from a time-iterated filter Riccati 0.000685/0.00217/0.00688/0.0219 (reported 0.00069/0.00217/0.00688/0.02194). Independent Monte Carlo of the cliff failure rate (own code, 20000 cycles, qd=1e-4, N=10, L=1446): 5.1% vs reported analytic 5.3% and reported simulation 2.9-3.7%. All agree. The derivation itself (bias-variance with linear drift regret) is standard so agreement is expected; reading the cost model as a whole is not checked against any outside tool (no published figure exists for this plant).
evidence.completeness: Every claimed result in the whitepaper (items 1-9) has a matching table in experiments/results.txt (sections 1-8) and the numbers quoted in the paper match those tables (checked 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and the safe-schedule N/T of item 7). README commands exist (tests 10, ~4 s as stated; run.py not re-run, ~4 min). experiments/figure.py and excess_vs_drift.svg exist. No stubs or TODOs found. Not done: the limitation 'dither on top of the controller' is stated as not modelled, which is the practical case. No programme entry in research/PROGRAMMES.md for this slug.
evidence.verification: Test command above: 10 pass. Seeded two mutations in src/twin_recalibration/model.py cycle_excess and reverted (git status clean): (1) drift-regret term `qd*L*(L+1)/2` changed to `qd*L*(L-1)/2`: all 10 tests still passed; (2) experiment cost multiplied by 1.1 in the exact-cost branch: all 10 still passed. So the full-model objective that produces the paper's safe-schedule and full-model numbers (results sections 1 full-model columns, 5, 6, 7) is guarded only by a 25% tolerance simulation test and the idealised tests. Tests that do bite: closed-form stationary point, equal thirds, window variance enumeration, regret-coefficient quadrature, cliff boundary. No test for the numbers in results.txt, for fail_prob against a simulation, or for kalman_regret.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (188 lines), test_model.py, run.py, pyproject.toml. Pure stdlib, clear docstrings that state the maths. Defects: no input validation (|a|>=1 makes exp_step_cost and exp_cycle_cost divide by zero or give negative variance silently; qd=0 gives ZeroDivision in closed_form); simulate() floors the estimate with `max(ys/us, 0.2)` silently and uses a 1e4 divergence threshold without reporting it in the return value beyond the failure fraction; fail_prob uses a fixed 601-point grid (m=120 inside best_schedule) with no convergence check; best_schedule ternary search assumes unimodality over L and, with a max_fail filter returning inf, can mis-order comparisons; very dense one-line code with lambdas; ~4 min experiment run.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: closed-form T*, N*, excess (model.py closed_form, results sec 1); equal thirds (sec 2); slopes 0.333/-0.664/-0.328 and c^(1/3) slope 0.336 (sec 3); robustness 26%/19% (sec 4, formula matched to 3 digits); 0.7-15% failure and 1.2x/3.6x/16x safe cost (sec 5, 7); sim-vs-model including the tail-dominated 159.5 mean at qd=1e-4 is disclosed in the paper (item 8) rather than hidden. Weak points: the headline '37-200x worse than the always-on Kalman twin' compares a failure-constrained batch schedule with an unconstrained Kalman twin whose own cliff risk is never computed; the stated 'stylised' label discloses that a=0.9, q=1, r=0.1, sigma^2=1 are chosen, not sourced (CLAUDE.md asks for sourced parameters); the 'relevance' paragraph for digital-twin maintenance is an extrapolation from one scalar plant. Whitepaper has no disclaimer-style limits beyond the Limitations section, which is honest.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: the code is small and importable and the closed-form law is verifiable. Nearest prior work, judged from the paper's own references and standard texts (no live literature search was run in this audit): the bias-variance trade-off for re-identification interval and experiment length is classical in adaptive/dual control and optimal experiment design (Astrom-Wittenmark, Ljung, Bar-Shalom), the sqrt-regret and stabilising-neighbourhood issues are in Dean et al. 2020 and Simchowitz-Foster 2020, and the cube-root law is the same structure as the Young/Daly checkpoint interval the paper cites. New here: the explicit constants for this LQ plant, the equal-thirds identity, and the quantified cost of the stability cliff. These are modest, correct, and not publishable at a controls venue in this form (scalar, one parameter, stable open-loop plant, no real data, no comparison to in-loop dither which is the practitioner's actual choice). Does not meet the research/CLAUDE.md PhD+ and deep-tech bar (no programme, no named venue, no real data or industrial tool).
evidence.domain: A system-identification practitioner would first ask why the experiment is open loop and why the comparator has no dither or in-loop excitation; the paper admits this in Limitations but the headline '37-200x worse than always-on' is then largely an artefact of the open-loop price c0=4.19 per step, which only exists because the plant is stable (a=0.9) and may be left open. Real twins also recalibrate on events and on change detection, not on a fixed interval, and the gain is not re-centred at each cycle. Departs from practice: fixed periodic schedule, scalar parameter known a, random-walk drift with a forced reset. Standard certainty-equivalent LQ is respected, the second-order regret treatment is right, and the first-passage treatment of the cliff is sound (upper bound, stated).

defects.what: Full-model cycle_excess (exact experiment cost, drift regret term) is not pinned by any test: seeded mutations of the L(L+1)/2 drift term and of the experiment cost x1.1 both left all 10 tests green, yet results sec 1 (full model), 5, 6, 7 depend on them

The 37-200x 'price of not using operating data' compares a failure-probability-constrained batch schedule with an unconstrained Kalman twin; the Kalman twin's own destabilisation risk is not computed, so the safe ratio is not like for like

Result is a scalar, stable-plant, open-loop-experiment model with chosen (not sourced) parameters and no real data or comparison against in-loop dither; below the PhD+/deep-tech bar in research/CLAUDE.md and not attached to any programme in PROGRAMMES.md
No input validation: |a|>=1 or qd=0 silently produce wrong values or ZeroDivisionError; simulate floors the estimate at 0.2 silently
fail_prob uses a fixed grid (m=120 in the optimiser) with no convergence check and best_schedule's ternary search over L assumes unimodality while mapping infeasible points to inf

Mean simulated excess at qd=1e-4 safe schedule is 159.5 (heavy tail); the table reports it, the paper explains it, but no median or trimmed statistic is produced to back 'treat the quoted excess as the typical cost'

verdict: The numbers are right: nine independently recomputed quantities (rho, c, T*, N*, excess, cliff, Kalman regret, equal-thirds terms, and a Monte Carlo failure rate) agree with the paper and results.txt to the printed precision, and the paper discloses its own tail and idealisation problems. It is honest, finished against its own claims, and small. It does not meet the bar: verification scores 2 because two seeded mutations in the full-model cost survived all 10 tests, and as research it is a correct but classical bias-variance result for one scalar stable plant with chosen parameters, a headline ratio against an unconstrained comparator, no real data, and no programme or venue, so fitness and domain score 2 against the PhD+ brief.
